subject: c10-sci

weightage.label: Unit I: Chemical Substances — board-assessed portion (Ch 1)

note: Official 2026-27 annual-exam unit marks: Chemical Substances 25, World of Living 25, Natural Phenomena 12, Effects of Current 13, Natural Resources 5; total 80, internal assessment 20. Acids, Bases and Salts; Metals and Non-metals; Carbon and its Compounds; and Evolution are explicitly identified as formative-only in the annual-exam structure. The formula/reference file therefore keeps only useful board-relevant formula material and excludes the formative-only Evolution chapter.

reference.label: Chemical equations
reference.text: Use the correct reactants/products and balance atoms on both sides. Identify combination, decomposition, displacement and double-displacement patterns from the reaction itself.

reference.label: Oxidation and reduction
reference.text: At this level, remember oxidation as addition of oxygen/removal of hydrogen and reduction as removal of oxygen/addition of hydrogen; both occur together in a redox reaction.

reference.label: Life processes
reference.text: For biology processes, learn the sequence and function: nutrition → respiration → transport → excretion. Pair every process with its key organ/structure and role.

reference.label: Control and coordination
reference.text: Reflex arc: receptor → sensory neuron → relay neuron → motor neuron → effector. Distinguish nervous control from hormonal control.

reference.label: Reproduction and heredity
reference.text: Keep a clear distinction between asexual and sexual reproduction, gamete formation, fertilisation and inheritance. For Mendelian monohybrid crosses, track genotype and phenotype separately.

reference.label: Light
reference.text: Use the mirror/lens sign convention consistently. Keep the mirror formula, lens formula, magnification and power relationships together and draw the ray diagram when useful.

reference.label: Human eye
reference.text: Normal eye: near point ≈ 25 cm and far point at infinity. Understand accommodation as change in focal length to focus at different distances.

reference.label: Electricity
reference.text: I = Q/t, V = W/Q, V = IR, R = ρl/A, series resistances add, parallel conductances add, P = VI = I²R = V²/R, and electrical energy E = Pt.

reference.label: Magnetic effects
reference.text: For a current-carrying conductor, the force depends on magnetic field, current and conductor length; remember Fleming's left-hand rule for direction.

reference.label: Our Environment
reference.text: Energy flows Sun → producers → consumers; only a small fraction is transferred to the next trophic level. Distinguish biodegradable from non-biodegradable waste.

mistakes: Chemical equations: balance atoms, preserve chemical formulas and write conditions/catalysts only where required.
Ray diagrams and electricity numericals: write the convention/formula first, substitute carefully and include units.
Biology: do not confuse structure, function and process; use labelled diagrams where they clarify the answer.
Heredity: keep genotype and phenotype separate and do not confuse dominant expression with frequency in a population.
Case-based and assertion-reason questions: test each statement against the scientific concept before selecting an option.
order: World of Living and the board-assessed part of Chemical Substances first: together these units carry 50 of 80 marks.
Then Effects of Current (13 marks): Electricity → Magnetic Effects.
Then Natural Phenomena (12 marks): Light → Human Eye.
Finish with Our Environment (5 marks), then use mixed questions to connect concepts across units.
Study the formative-only chapters for school learning, but do not count them as annual-board marks.
